label: DAILY EDITION
title: Three things worth knowing
subtitle: A Phase III obesity treatment result, completed worker-rights remedies and a new global restoration baseline.

stories.title: Phase III retatrutide trial cut average weight by 18.8% at 80 weeks
stories.text: In a randomized trial of 2,047 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, the 12 mg weekly dose reduced average body weight by 18.8%, versus 5.1% with placebo. Seventy-two percent reached an HbA1c of 6.5% or lower.
stories.why: The results point to another potentially effective option for people managing both obesity and diabetes. Retatrutide is not approved, the study was funded by its maker Eli Lilly, and gastrointestinal side effects were common.

stories.title: Akwel reinstated three workers with full backpay after a labor-rights case
stories.text: A remediation plan at Akwel’s Ciudad Juárez plant reinstated three workers with full backpay and benefits and paid full severance to six others. The company also restructured labor management and introduced annual rights training and a confidential complaint channel.
stories.why: The measures provide direct remedies and stronger protections after authorities found interference with organizing rights. The outcome covers one facility, and lasting improvement will depend on continued monitoring and enforcement.
stories.source: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative · 28 Sep 2026

stories.title: 62 countries report 206.5 million hectares under restoration
stories.text: New FAO analysis says 62 countries have reported about 206.5 million hectares of forests and landscapes under restoration—around 44% of the estimated global terrestrial area needed to meet the 2030 biodiversity target.
stories.why: It provides the clearest baseline yet showing restoration at significant scale. “Under restoration” does not mean recovery is complete, reporting methods vary, and about 56% of the estimated need remains.
